question: How do CCSD(T) and M06-2X methodologies compare in calculating thermochemical properties and reaction kinetics for hydrazine and oxygen reactions?
answer: For geometry optimizations and vibrational analyses, the M06-2X density functional with the maug-cc-pVTZ basis set was used.  Energetic properties were then refined using CCSD(T) with the aug-cc-pVTZ basis set, based on the M06-2X geometries.  This dual-level approach was employed to calculate minimum energy paths and kinetic properties, including rate constants with variational transition state theory and tunneling corrections.  The T1 diagnostic was used to validate the applicability of CCSD(T).

The purpose of the paper is to develop and validate a theoretical model that explains the temperature-dependent kinetics of the reaction between hydrazine (N₂H₄) and oxygen, particularly in hydrazine-rich environments. The model incorporates quantum chemical calculations and kinetic theory to account for experimental observations, including the unusual negative temperature dependence of the rate constant in certain conditions. The study emphasizes the importance of the hydrazine dimer in accurately describing the reaction mechanism and improving the understanding of the global N₂H₄ combustion process.
